newsitem.title: UK: UK assets retain allure despite EMU risk - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK assets retain allure despite EMU risk - poll.

text.p: MONTH US UK GER FRA EURO JAPAN ASIA LATAM CASH

* = Balance in commodities # = Balance in sector holdings

Despite last week's European Commission statistics that revealed Britain along with Greece and Italy would fail to meet the Maastricht criteria on European Monetary Union, investors polled in Reuters monthly asset allocation survey remain sanguine on UK assets. They have increased exposure to gilts from 8.4 percent of a global bond fund in October to 9.7 percent in November.
"It is completely ridiculous to place British assets in the same risk class as Italy," said one fund manager.
Funds are also increasing allocations throughout Europe, with countries other than France and Germany seeing a rise to 24.9 percent of a global bond fund from 23.6 percent in October.
The main loser is U.S. Treasuries, down from 34.9 percent of a global bond fund in October to just 31 percent now.

"With a cap now being put on the dollar, the risk for Japanese investors incurring currency losses on the U.S. Treasuries bought over the last six months will catalyse a withdrawal from dollars, reinforcing the dollar downturn we already see," Kleinwort Benson strategist Albert Edwards said.
Japan is also a loser, from 10.6 percent to 7.6 percent of a global bond fund.
Cash has been hiked from 2.1 percent to 3.9 percent of a global bond portfolio by nervous investors.

Among global equity markets, the rate of selling down the U.S. and Canada has accelerated, with allocations at 25 percent of a global equity fund, against 29.9 percent in October and 30.3 percent in September.
This weighting compares with 42.8 percent for the U.S. alone in benchmark FTA World Index.
Cash has also been raised in this asset class, up to 3.6 percent from 2.8 percent in October and 1.8 percent in September.
"The risks of a global equity bear market have increased sharply. We would advise clients to take extreme care over the next few months in equities," said Kleinwort's Edwards.
Kleinwort prefers both bonds and cash to equities and cash is now 15 percent of its model equity portfolio, its maximum level.
Again, the UK market is a net gainer, with allocations in a global equity fund up from 9.6 percent in October and 10.6 percent in September to 12.5 percent now.
Exposure to European equities has also been raised, Germany to 6.6 percent from 5.4 percent, France to 4.2 percent from 4.0 percent and other Europe to 16.0 percent from 13.4 percent.
Japan is about unchanged at 21.6 percent of a global equity fund from 21.3 percent last month, while emerging markets, exluding Asia Pacific, have been cut to 2.0 percent from 3.0 percent last month.
Asia Pacific is down to 9.0 percent from 10.4 percent. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
